type:
∀ φ : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Part _root_.Nat,
  _root_.AcceptableNumbering φ →
  let K : _root_.Set _root_.Nat := {n |
    let p := _root_.Nat.unpair n
    _root_.Part.Dom (φ (_root_.Prod.fst p) (_root_.Prod.snd p))}
  let sigmaOne : _root_.Set _root_.Nat → Prop := fun A =>
    _root_.Set.preimage (fun xs : _root_.Fin 1 → _root_.Nat => xs 0) A ∈
      _root_.Prod.fst (_root_.ArithmeticalHierarchyLevels 1 1 (_root_.Nat.le_refl 1))
  sigmaOne K ∧
    ∀ A : _root_.Set _root_.Nat, sigmaOne A →
      ∃ f : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat, _root_.Computable f ∧
        ∀ n : _root_.Nat, n ∈ A ↔ f n ∈ K
sourceReason: Only Alphabeta Math’s shared-library item thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete states this endpoint. The translation uses Nat.pair as the fixed computable bijective pairing, decoded by Nat.unpair. The linked definition of completeness requires Sigma-1 membership and a total computable many-one reduction from each Sigma-1 set. The article-specific Research Portal and defect report both returned HTTP 404, so no correction could be verified. https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-halting-is-sigma-one-complete https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-arithmetical-level-completeness https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
